name: Preparation for Optical Analysis
description: Preparation of IC samples specifically for optical microscopy and imaging. Covers achieving mirror-finish polish on target layers, contrast enhancement techniques (decorative etching, staining, interference-layer methods), correct sample mounting for microscope stages, illumination mode preparation (brightfield, darkfield, DIC/Nomarski, polarized light), and progressive delayering with inter-layer documentation for reverse engineering. Goal: high-quality optical micrographs for layer extraction, defect analysis, or documentation.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to optical sample preparation

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the relationship between preparation quality and optical imaging results
evidence: Can explain how surface finish affects image quality under different illumination modes
Understands the purpose of contrast enhancement techniques for semiconductor imaging
Aware of the optical microscope capabilities and limitations for IC analysis

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Prepares standard samples to optical-grade finish under supervision
evidence: Achieves scratch-free mirror polish on single-layer planar samples
Performs basic Dash or Secco etch for junction delineation under guidance
Mounts samples correctly for compound microscope with appropriate coverslipping or stub
Captures usable micrographs under brightfield illumination

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently prepares samples for high-quality optical analysis across illumination modes
evidence: Selects and applies appropriate contrast enhancement (stain, etch, interference) for target layer and feature type
Performs progressive delayering with optical documentation at each layer for reverse engineering
Achieves consistent preparation quality across multiple samples in a batch
Produces optical micrographs with sufficient quality for gate-level netlist extraction or reporting

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles advanced process nodes and develops preparation-imaging workflows
evidence: Prepares advanced-node samples whose feature pitch falls below the optical diffraction limit, delivering them for SEM-based imaging rather than optical readout
Develops end-to-end delayer-image-stitch workflows for full-die optical reverse engineering
Optimizes contrast enhancement recipes for specific foundry processes and technology nodes
Mentors team on preparation quality targets and imaging workflow optimization

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines optical preparation methodology; integrates with automated imaging systems
evidence: Defines lab SOPs for optical preparation and acceptance criteria for image quality
Specifies and integrates automated stitching microscope systems for large-area imaging
Develops preparation techniques for emerging node technologies and novel IC structures
Trains teams and conducts proficiency assessments for optical preparation operators

assessment_methods.description: Prepare a decapped IC sample and produce optical micrographs of at least 3 metal layers with documented contrast enhancement at each level
Review a set of layer micrographs for image quality, focus, contrast, and completeness of layer documentation

equipment: Compound optical microscope with DIC/Nomarski, darkfield, and polarized light capability
Automated optical inspection / stitching microscope (e.g., Zeiss Axio Imager with motorized stage)
Semi-automatic polishing system for controlled material removal
